description: Real NASA imagery for the Solar System intro. Rebuild with: npm run data:intro
policy: NASA sources only. NASA imagery is generally not subject to copyright in the United States; credits follow NASA media usage guidelines.

sun.png.subject: The Sun in extreme ultraviolet (171 Å)
sun.png.mission: Solar Dynamics Observatory, Atmospheric Imaging Assembly
sun.png.credit: NASA/SDO and the AIA science team
processing: Square crop of 1028 px around the Sun, resized to 256 px
Black space made transparent; the corona fades out at 0.86–0.99 of the half-width

earth.jpg.subject: Earth
earth.jpg.mission: DSCOVR EPIC (Earth Polychromatic Imaging Camera), from 1.5 million km
processing: Square crop to the disc, resized to 1024 px

mercury.jpg.title: PIA15160: Mercury Globe: 0°N, 0°E
mercury.jpg.credit: NASA/Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory/Carnegie Institution of Washington
processing: Square crop to the planet's disc, resized to 160 px

venus.jpg.subject: Venus
venus.jpg.title: PIA23791: Venus from Mariner 10
processing: Square crop to the planet's disc (left panel), resized to 160 px

mars.jpg.subject: Mars
mars.jpg.title: PIA00407: Global Color Views of Mars
processing: Square crop to the planet's disc, resized to 160 px

jupiter.jpg.subject: Jupiter

Black space made transparent; the planet's disc stays opaque

processing: Square crop to the planet's disc, resized to 160 px

neptune.jpg.subject: Neptune

sky-south-ecliptic-pole.jpg.subject: The sky around the south ecliptic pole, behind the Sun in a view from above the Solar System
sky-south-ecliptic-pole.jpg.credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech (SPHEREx); HiPS by the SPHEREx Science Data Center, Caltech/IPAC
processing: Stereographic projection centred on the south ecliptic pole (J2000 ecliptic, obliquity 23.4392911°), seen from inside the sky
Ecliptic longitude 0° (March equinox) to the right, 90° up: the orientation of the intro orrery
2048×2048 px, 70° from the centre to the middle of each edge, 3×3 samples per pixel
Display stretch: black point at the 35th percentile (3.9), white at the 99.95th (189.2), gamma 0.9
2400 pixels have no data in the DR1 all-sky HiPS (a disc of about 2.2° radius at the pole); they show the local median sky level and sit behind the Sun
